symmetry

/SIM-ih-tree/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Symmetry means a balanced arrangement in which one half or side is an exact, mirrored match of the other.

The cathedral's facade was prized for its perfect symmetry, with matching towers rising on either side of the entrance.

Example

A face-recognition researcher explained that humans across cultures consistently rate faces with near-perfect left-right symmetry as more attractive, even when study participants can't consciously identify why one photo appeals to them more than another.

The researcher is describing a specific, measurable balance between the two halves of a face — exactly what "symmetry" names, whether in faces, buildings, or any other shape.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

regularity: Regularity stresses a consistent, evenly repeated pattern — columns at equal intervals, stripes of equal width. Symmetry makes a different demand: that one side mirror the other around a center. A repeating wallpaper has regularity; a butterfly's wings have symmetry.

harmony: Harmony is the felt agreement of parts — colors, shapes, and sizes that simply work together. Symmetry is objective and checkable: fold the design at its center and the halves must match. A room can be harmonious with nothing mirrored in it.

evenness: Evenness means uniform level or distribution — even lighting, an even coat of paint, with no lumps or gaps. Symmetry is stricter and more structural: not sameness throughout, but an exact mirrored correspondence between two sides.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

asymmetry: the direct opposite — unevenness between two sides

lopsidedness: a more casual word for an unbalanced, uneven arrangement

Where it sits · how exactly the two sides match

balance → proportion → symmetry

balance vs. symmetry: Balance is weaker than symmetry: a room can feel roughly balanced without any exact matching, while symmetry goes further, demanding that one side mirror the other precisely.

proportion vs. symmetry: Proportion is milder than symmetry: good proportion only asks that a room's parts feel harmonious together, while symmetry makes the heavier demand of an exact, mirrored match between the two sides.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — sym-: together, same (Greek syn-)

Root — metr-: measure (Greek metron)

Suffix — -y: noun-forming

Put it together: "symmetry" literally means "measured together" or "same measure" — sym- signals sameness, while metr- refers to measurement, describing two sides measured and found to match exactly.

Use the root in a new word: geometry: Students used geometry to calculate the exact angles needed for the bridge's triangular supports.

Word Choice

neutral, technical/artistic

Symmetry is a neutral, precise word used across art, architecture, biology, and mathematics. It describes an objective, often measurable balance, rather than a vague impression of niceness.
